chapters: After spotting a limping cottontail bedding under the hot hive row, Maeve sneaks out after dark and slips romaine beneath the pallets, hiding the wrappers in the warm room.
Eli tightens the electric fence, smears bacon-greased foil on corners, runs mite washes by the book, and updates his expense spiral after confirming the charger is hot.
Aiden posts a dusk reel of the rabbit under the hives that draws strangers with snacks, and when Eli confronts him in the drive, Maeve pockets dropped carrot tops and says nothing.
act_scenes:
Chapter 1:
Scene 1:
Characters: Maeve
Place: Apiary—hot hive row
Time: Late afternoon, Day 1
Event: Maeve spots a limping cottontail bedding under the pallets; she watches bees, studies the rabbit’s path, decides to help.
Conflict: Compassion vs farm rules and biosecurity
Story value: Secrecy/Trust
Story value charge: Negative (secret begins)
Mood: Careful, watchful
Outcome: Maeve resolves to sneak food later.

Scene 2:
Characters: Maeve
Place: Apiary, then warm room
Time: After lights-out, Night 1
Event: Maeve slips romaine under pallets, checks the rabbit’s breathing, hides produce wrappers in the warm room.
Conflict: Avoiding detection vs doing the “right” thing
Story value: Secrecy/Trust
Story value charge: More negative (deeper deception)
Mood: Furtive, tense
Outcome: Rabbit fed; evidence hidden.

Chapter 2:
Scene 1:
Characters: Eli
Place: Pasture perimeter and hive yard
Time: Morning, Day 2
Event: Eli tightens electric fence, greases foil with bacon on corners, tests charger, runs mite washes by the book.
Conflict: Threat of predators and pests vs control through procedure
Story value: Control/Order
Story value charge: Positive (systems tightened)
Mood: Methodical, wary
Outcome: Fence hot, deterrents up, mite counts logged.

Scene 2:
Characters: Eli
Place: Kitchen table/office nook
Time: Evening, Day 2
Event: Eli updates the expense spiral, reconciles receipts, notes margins; flags upcoming feed and fuel costs.
Conflict: Financial pressure vs disciplined record-keeping
Story value: Stability/Strain
Story value charge: Slightly negative (numbers tighten)
Mood: Tired, pragmatic
Outcome: Books balanced; strain acknowledged.

Chapter 3:
Scene 1:
Characters: Aiden
Place: Apiary edge and phone screen
Time: Dusk, Day 3
Event: Aiden films and posts a reel of the rabbit under the hives; tags location loosely; comments roll in, locals ask if they can bring snacks.
Conflict: Engagement/clout vs privacy/safety
Story value: Exposure/Safety
Story value charge: Negative (exposure spikes)
Mood: Buzzed, careless
Outcome: Post gains traction; visitors primed.

Scene 2:
Characters: Eli, Aiden, Maeve
Place: Driveway by the barn
Time: Night, Day 3
Event: A car idles in the drive with people holding snacks; Eli confronts Aiden; Maeve pockets dropped carrot tops and stays silent.
Conflict: Authority vs deflection; loyalty vs honesty
Story value: Family Unity/Fracture
Story value charge: Negative (trust frays)
Mood: Heated, awkward
Outcome: Aiden chastised; visitors turned away; Maeve’s secret deepens.

chapters: Warden Gary issues a feeding warning and tests the fence while Henry sets traps, Eli wrenches his shoulder during a pull, and he writes the new losses into his spiral.
Maeve brings Lila by headlamp to remove the botfly and lay out brush-cover steps, then dumps her feed stash and sweeps spilled cappings.
Aiden’s drone and Soot flush the rabbit, Maeve slips parsley under a block, and a young bear pops a corner post, knocks lids, chills brood, and leaves Eli sniffing greens on the pallets.
act_scenes:
Chapter 4:
Scene 1:
Characters: Warden Gary, Henry, Eli
Place: South fence line and pasture edge
Time: Early morning, day after latest loss
Event: Gary issues a wildlife-feeding warning, tests the hot fence; Henry sets two footholds and a snare; Eli walks the line with them.
Conflict: Enforcement vs. livelihood methods; citation risk vs. needed deterrence
Story value: Compliance vs. Violation
Story value charge: Negative
Mood: Tight, procedural
Outcome: Written warning posted; fence reads weak on the far span; traps placed under Gary’s conditions; tension rises.

Scene 2:
Characters: Eli
Place: Apiary and kitchen table
Time: Late afternoon into dusk
Event: Eli wrenches his shoulder lifting a heavy super during a pull; later he logs fresh losses in his spiral notebook.
Conflict: Body limits vs. workload; denial vs. accounting
Story value: Health vs. Injury; Optimism vs. Attrition
Story value charge: Negative
Mood: Gritted, tired
Outcome: Shoulder strained and taped; losses tallied; morale dips.

Chapter 5:
Scene 1:
Characters: Maeve, Lila
Place: Mudroom workbench, then fence corridor
Time: Night, by headlamp
Event: Lila extracts a botfly larva from the barn cat with Maeve assisting; they map brush-cover steps along the fence to redirect small game movement.
Conflict: Squeamishness vs. necessity; stopgap fixes vs. systemic prevention
Story value: Health vs. Infestation; Control vs. Drift
Story value charge: Positive
Mood: Clinical, focused
Outcome: Wound flushed and dressed; brush piles and corridors sketched with flagged stakes.

Scene 2:
Characters: Maeve
Place: Feed shed and honey room
Time: Pre-dawn
Event: She dumps her secret feed stash, bins the rest in sealed drums, and sweeps up spilled cappings and crumbs to cut attractants.
Conflict: Convenience vs. risk; hoarding vs. hardening
Story value: Resources vs. Security
Story value charge: Positive
Mood: Resigned, methodical
Outcome: Attractants removed; storage tightened; short-term loss for lowered draw.

Chapter 6:
Scene 1:
Characters: Aiden, Maeve, Soot (dog)
Place: Garden edge and hedgerow
Time: Morning
Event: Aiden flies a drone while Soot works the scent; they flush a rabbit; Maeve slips parsley under a cinder block to pattern its return path.
Conflict: Tech/noise vs. animal wariness; competing tactics under time pressure
Story value: Control vs. Evasion
Story value charge: Slight Positive
Mood: Brisk, tactical
Outcome: Rabbit route identified; low-key bait set without spooking the warren.

Scene 2:
Characters: Eli
Place: Apiary
Time: Night attack; dawn assessment
Event: A young bear pops a corner post, knocks lids, chills brood; by morning Eli walks the pallets, shoulder aching, and catches the scent of greens.
Conflict: Human defenses vs. wild force; livelihood vs. predation
Story value: Security vs. Breach; Livelihood vs. Loss
Story value charge: Negative
Mood: Gut-punched, contained
Outcome: Corner post down; two colonies compromised; repairs queued; faint parsley scent on pallets noted.

act_scenes:
Chapter 7:
Scene 1:
Characters: Maeve, Eli, Lila (on speaker)
Place: Apiary yard by the hives
Time: Same night, ~9:30 p.m.
Event: Maeve admits she’s been feeding the rabbit. Eli cools off, sets the flashlight down, calls Lila on speaker. They agree to stop feeding and to build brush cover in the morning.
Conflict: Trust strained vs. need to act together
Story value: Trust
Story value charge: Positive
Mood: Tense but cooperative
Outcome: Unified plan and boundary set (no more feeding; brush cover tomorrow)

Scene 2:
Characters: Maeve, Eli, young bear (unseen), Gary, Aiden (via post), Mara
Place: Apiary and house; texts/calls
Time: Overnight to late morning
Event: A young bear folds a corner post, pops two hive lids, chilling brood. Morning brings a written warning from Gary triggered by Aiden’s social post; Mara threatens to shift shelf space if issues continue.
Conflict: Wildlife hit and public scrutiny vs. limited resources and reputation
Story value: Security of livelihood
Story value charge: Negative
Mood: Jangled, defensive
Outcome: Brood loss, fence damage, formal warning, retail pressure escalates

Chapter 8:
Scene 1:
Characters: Maeve, Eli, Lila, co‑op rep, rabbit
Place: Apiary and bottling shed
Time: First frost day, dawn to dusk
Event: They strip all attractants, tighten the electric fence hot, finish dense brush cover, pull a smaller clean harvest, bottle, and see the rabbit slip into the new cover. The co‑op confirms a steady allotment.
Conflict: Time and cold vs. doing it right under scrutiny
Story value: Stability
Story value charge: Positive
Mood: Spare, focused, relieved
Outcome: Hardening of defenses, ethical fix for the rabbit, smaller but clean product, market stability secured
